items.title: 9.5.1 Calculating H3O+ ions from Ka and the molar concentration of a weak acid

source_refs.note: Topic 9.5.1 with Sample 9.3, printed pages 196-197. The print's '0.18 x 10^-6' is corrected to 1.8 x 10^-6 and noted.

blocks.text: Weak acids do not completely dissociate in water, so the hydronium ion concentration is not equal to the initial concentration of the acid; the equilibrium expression is used instead. For a weak acid HA the dissociation is HA(aq) gives H+(aq) + A-(aq), and in water H+ combines with water to form H3O+, so the equilibrium in terms of H3O+ is HA(aq) gives H3O+(aq) + A-(aq). Let the initial concentration of HA be C mol dm-3. At equilibrium [H3O+] = x, [A-] = x and [HA] = C - x, so Ka = [H3O+][A-] / [HA] = x^2 / (C - x). For weak acids x is usually very small compared with C, so C - x is approximately C and the expression simplifies to Ka = x^2 / C. Taking the square root of both sides, x = the square root of (Ka x C), so the concentration of H3O+ is the square root of (Ka C).

Calculate [H3O+] in a 0.1 M solution of acetic acid, Ka = 1.8 x 10^-5. [H3O+] = the square root of (Ka C) = the square root of (1.8 x 10^-5 x 0.1) = the square root of (1.8 x 10^-6) = 1.34 x 10^-3 M. (The print shows the product as 0.18 x 10^-6; it is 1.8 x 10^-6.) The hydronium concentration is approximately 1.34 x 10^-3 mol dm-3.

blocks.prompt: Calculate [H3O+] in 0.1 M nitrous acid, Ka = 4 x 10^-4, and find Ka for formic acid if 0.10 M HCOOH has pH 2.38 (Quick Check 9.3a, b).
blocks.explanation: Nitrous acid: [H3O+] = the square root of (4 x 10^-4 x 0.1) = the square root of (4 x 10^-5) = 6.3 x 10^-3 mol dm-3 (about 6 per cent of C, so the approximation is only rough). Formic acid: [H3O+] = 10^-2.38 = 4.2 x 10^-3 mol dm-3, so Ka = x^2 / (C - x) = (4.2 x 10^-3)^2 / (0.10 - 0.0042) = 1.76 x 10^-5 / 0.0958 = 1.8 x 10^-4.

items: For a weak acid of concentration C: [H3O+] = [A-] = x, [HA] = C - x, Ka = x^2 / (C - x) which simplifies to x^2 / C, so [H3O+] = the square root of (Ka C).
Sample 9.3: 0.1 M acetic acid, Ka 1.8 x 10^-5, gives [H3O+] = the square root of (1.8 x 10^-6) = 1.34 x 10^-3 mol dm-3.
